title: Possessive Adjectives - My, Your, His, Her
description: Show who owns what: 'my book', 'his cat', 'their house' - essential vocabulary!
can_do: Show ownership (my cat, your house, his book, their car)
Use possessive adjectives with correct gender agreement
Say 'Where is my book?' or 'I want your car' in French

vocabulary.note: masculine form - mon livre, mon père, mon ami
feminine form - ma maison, ma mère, ma voiture
plural form - mes chats, mes livres, mes amis
masculine form - ton chat, ton frère, ton travail
feminine form - ta voiture, ta sœur, ta chambre
plural form - tes amis, tes parents, tes chaussures
masculine form - son livre, son chien, son bureau
feminine form - sa maison, sa fille, sa cuisine
plural form - ses chats, ses enfants, ses clés
singular form - notre maison, notre école, notre jardin
plural form - nos chats, nos vacances, nos professeurs
singular form - votre livre, votre famille, votre bureau
plural form - vos livres, vos enfants, vos bagages
singular form - leur chat, leur maison, leur projet
plural form - leurs chats, leurs amis, leurs idées

concepts.definition: Words that show ownership and go directly before the noun they modify
concepts.example: 15 total forms: MY ({mon}/{ma}/{mes}), YOUR informal ({ton}/{ta}/{tes}), HIS/HER ({son}/{sa}/{ses}), OUR ({notre}/{nos}), YOUR formal ({votre}/{vos}), THEIR ({leur}/{leurs})

concepts.term: 🔑 CRITICAL RULE: Agreement with the THING owned
concepts.definition: The possessive adjective matches the gender/number of the THING being owned, NOT the owner
concepts.example: Marie's book = {SON livre} (masculine '{son}' because '{livre}' is masculine, even though Marie is female). Pierre's house = {SA maison} (feminine '{sa}' because '{maison}' is feminine, even though Pierre is male)

concepts.definition: French has two ways to say 'your' depending on relationship and respect level
concepts.example: INFORMAL with friends/family: {ton}/{ta}/{tes} ({ton frère}, {ta sœur}, {tes amis}). FORMAL with strangers/respect: {votre}/{vos} ({votre bureau}, {vos bagages})

concepts.definition: Some possessives don't change for masculine/feminine - only for singular/plural
concepts.example: {NOTRE}/{NOS} (our): {notre maison}, {notre jardin}, {nos enfants. VOTRE}/{VOS} (your formal): {votre livre}, {votre famille}, {vos idées. LEUR}/{LEURS} (their): {leur chat}, {leur maison}, {leurs amis}

concepts.definition: Each owner has a predictable number of forms to memorize
concepts.example: MY, YOUR (informal), HIS/HER = 3 forms each (masc/fem/plural). OUR, YOUR (formal), THEIR = 2 forms each (singular/plural only)

items.situation: Talking about Marie's dog (masculine). Which possessive?
items.hint: Marie owns it, chien is masculine - matches the thing owned!

items.situation: Talking about Pierre's house (feminine). Which possessive?
items.hint: Pierre owns it, maison is feminine - matches the thing owned!
